sent:
Lena,

You said ads got expensive. Here’s the short teardown and three changes we’d make this week.

Where clicks leak now
- Paid traffic lands on the homepage; in our audits, homepages lose about half of paid clicks in the first five seconds.
- Currency/symbol encoding is broken (“Â£”, “â€“”, “â€¢”) in banners and price tiles—hurts trust at the decision point.
- The ring size guide lives on a separate page; shoppers leave product pages to find it and don’t always return.
- Free UK shipping starts at £75; many single-SKU orders (£38–£70) need a nudge to reach it.

Three fast fixes
1) One offer page per ad (start with your best-selling ring).
- Above the fold: clear promise (recycled silver, fits first time), price, size selector, “Find your size” popover (not a separate page), 4.8★ (180+ reviews) with 2–3 short quotes, “Free resizing in 30 days” and “Dispatches in 3–5 days,” one Add to Cart.
- Point ring ads to this page, not Home or a grid.

2) Lift AOV to the £75 threshold.
- On PDP and cart: live progress bar (“£X to free UK shipping”).
- “Stack this look” block with 1‑click add of a curated pair/trio that takes common single items to ≥£75.
- Prebuild a “Stacks & Gifts” collection to catch paid gifting clicks.

3) Fix trust placement and encoding.
- Declare UTF‑8 sitewide and remove double‑encoded characters so £, dashes and bullets render correctly everywhere.
- Surface “Free resizing,” “Dispatch in 3–5 days” and review stars within the first screen on PDPs and key collection tiles.
- If you run a first‑order discount, auto‑apply it on landing so the discounted price shows in cart without a code.

Creative to power the test
- Ship concepts in threes (e.g. stack-in-hand, “Made in Brighton,” recycled silver + free resizing). Three variants each. Retire any ad after three weeks of falling click‑through; keep climbers. Each concept points to its matching offer page.

What to count
- Count first orders and AOV per ad→page pair. Move budget to the pairs that produce the cheapest first orders; ignore clicks that don’t convert.
